title: No command exposes a bundle's active type vocabulary; the unknown-type warning doesn't name valid types either
description:
User ask, verbatim, relayed via opum-agent 2026-09-18: "make sure the help / instructions are
fully reviewed and updated so that the actual agents know how to use the functionality properly."
That applies to whatever ships from this task -- see AC#2.

THE GAP, measured against dev at HEAD (75a783a9):

1. No command reads out a bundle's active type vocabulary (the profile's declared types, their
base + type-specific fields, and required sections). `lore help` lists 26 commands; none do this.
The closest is `lore schema export` (src/commands/schema.ts) -- but that WRITES
`.lore/schemas/*.schema.json` files to disk and requires the caller to already know a type name to
inspect usefully. It is a file-materialization command, not a discovery command. An agent that hits
an unknown-type warning has no CLI path to ask "what types does this bundle actually support" short
of hand-reading `.lore/schemas/*.json` plus `.lore/profile.toml` and reconciling the two -- exactly
what opum-agent's predecessor had to do by hand while investigating LCLI-534.

2. The unknown-type warning itself doesn't help either. src/core/schema.ts:315:
   options.warnings?.add(`unknown type "${type}"${where}; validated on \`type\` only`);
names only the rejected value, never the valid set. src/core/profile.ts:81's own comment claims the
profile's `case` setting "powers the unknown-type \"did you mean\" hint" -- but no hint is actually
emitted anywhere in the unknown-type path (schema.ts:315 is the only emission site); grepping the
source for "did you mean" turns up only that one comment. Either the hint was never wired up or was
removed and the comment never updated -- either way, documented behavior and actual behavior disagree.

FIX SHAPE, not prescribed: a read-only command (working name `lore types`) that prints the active
profile's type vocabulary -- names, base vs type-specific fields, required sections -- and fixing
the unknown-type warning to name the valid set and/or a nearest-match suggestion, closing the gap
profile.ts:81 already claims exists.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A command exists that prints a bundle's active type vocabulary (every declared type, its base and type-specific fields, and required sections) without the caller needing to already know a type name or hand-read .lore/schemas/*.json.
The unknown-type warning (src/core/schema.ts:315 today) names the valid type set, a nearest-match suggestion, or both -- it no longer reports only the rejected value.

lore instructions (and any topic it touches) and lore help / lore <command> --help for the new or changed commands are updated to describe the new behavior, so an agent driving lore learns about it from the tool itself.
bun run lint, typecheck and the test suite pass, and lore check exits 0.
